summary: Add the canonical provider-neutral Social Core: editable Content masters, immutable ContentVariant publish snapshots, social ChannelAccount capability projections, host-owned UTC schedules, guarded Publication lifecycle/status evidence, released-upload references and additive Connector SDK v1 social publish/status/media interfaces.

impacts.evidence: All content, variants, media references, channel projections, publications and status history are organization/workspace scoped with explicit repository predicates, transaction-local scope, composite tenant foreign keys and forced RLS.

Social Core may hold business-authored publish copy but event/audit evidence excludes content bodies. Media stores only released UploadID references; provider payloads, credentials, object keys, signed URLs and raw errors are excluded.
Task 020 adds no REST/OpenAPI operation. The domain is consumed internally by later n8n/application surfaces.
Four new additive v1 social event payload schemas are registered; no existing event type or payload is changed.

Connector SDK major v1 root interfaces remain frozen. Additive capability-specific SocialPublisher, SocialPublicationStatusReader and MediaAccessor interfaces reuse the pre-existing exact social capability vocabulary.
Expand migration 000027 adds six forced-RLS Social Core tables and lifecycle/immutability guards with no backfill or destructive change.

Capability checks fail closed before provider execution, channel activation requires an active social connector account, released upload state is checked at variant creation and must be revalidated again before every media read, and remote secrets/storage locators are forbidden from Core.
Task 020 defines publish lifecycle and capability validation only. It does not weaken Task-017 approval policy; later high-risk social write policy remains an application/governance decision.

Every repository mutation appends Task-003 audit and Task-008 outbox evidence in the same transaction; publication mutations also append immutable status history with correlation/version/attempt data.

Immutable publish snapshots plus optimistic publication versions and monotonic attempt transitions prevent duplicate workers from claiming the same state transition. Provider remote IDs remain outside Core for later mapping/reconciliation work.
Social Core performs no arbitrary webhook/network egress. Provider HTTP remains behind the Connector Runtime transport boundary.
Publication status, attempt, bounded reason_code, correlation and immutable status events provide safe operational dimensions without provider payload/error cardinality.
The migration is additive and application rollback retains social records/evidence. No destructive down migration is required; later schema contraction must use Task-067 gates.

Deterministic domain/SDK tests cover media shapes, capability exactness, schedules/transitions, duplicate UploadID rejection and safe reasons; repository static tests cover RLS, released-media/capability/lifecycle guards, audit/outbox use and SDK vocabulary alignment.
